canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across papers, the prevailing usage treats privacy leakage as observable disclosure of sensitive, private, or personally identifiable information in model outputs. Most definitions count leakage when a model reveals protected content after adversarial prompting, prompt injection, or other manipulation, though some papers describe it under simple natural questions or under a good-faith assumption that any request is trustworthy. Success is variously defined as outputting protected information, reproducing memorized training content, inferring additional hidden fragments from a few known ones, or revealing all or part of a system prompt or access code; a smaller line defines leakage relative to context, such as disclosing information forbidden by a user-defined security policy or in situations where it should be withheld.

Variants. Frequently studied variants include prompt or system prompt extraction, PII leakage or extraction, training-data-focused leakage such as training data extraction and fragment inference, and agent-side data stealing or full request leakage. Other papers place the behavior in generated summaries, in reasoning traces as well as final answers, in simple non-adversarial question answering, or in multimodal settings where both a private image and its associated text are exposed.

Space of elicitation and scores. Papers link this behavior to 5 measurement instruments, most often Membership inference attack, followed by DecodingTrust, InjecAgent, MUSE, and Mind2Web. These instruments span privacy auditing attacks, benchmarks, and datasets: Membership inference attack is used to evaluate member versus non-member differences and membership leakage, DecodingTrust is used through an Enron email extraction task, InjecAgent tests direct harm and data stealing attacks, MUSE includes no privacy leakage as one of its evaluation properties, and Mind2Web is used for action steps involving diverse PII categories on realistic websites.

What it is taken as evidence of. Papers link privacy leakage to 3 constructs. The most common construct-level link is to memorization: papers claim a causal relationship from memorization to privacy leakage, describing leakage as arising when models memorize training data verbatim or when PII embedded in training data can be extracted. Privacy leakage is also used to measure privacy preservation and is otherwise reported as related to it, while one paper reports it is related to generation diversity through reduced leakage risk without compromising diversity.

definitions.text: The observable act of using a small set of known text fragments from a training sample to infer additional, unknown fragments from the same sample by querying a model.
definitions.paper: Fragments to Facts: Partial-Information Fragment Inference from LLMs

definitions.text: An observable attack behavior where the model is manipulated into revealing its confidential system instructions or prompts.
definitions.paper: The Illusion of Role Separation: Hidden Shortcuts in LLM Role Learning (and How to Fix Them)

definitions.text: Revealing sensitive information as a result of malicious prompt injection or adversarial manipulation.
definitions.paper: AdvAgent: Controllable Blackbox Red-teaming on Web Agents

definitions.text: The malicious act of accessing and exfiltrating sensitive or private information, such as emails or payment methods.
definitions.paper: UDora: A Unified Red Teaming Framework against LLM Agents by Dynamically Hijacking Their Own Reasoning

definitions.text: The unintended disclosure of hazardous or private knowledge in either final answers or reasoning traces, despite unlearning attempts.
definitions.paper: Reasoning Model Unlearning: Forgetting Traces, Not Just Answers, While Preserving Reasoning Skills

definitions.text: The observable reproduction of sensitive or personally identifiable information from training data in model outputs.
definitions.paper: Interpretation Meets Safety: A Survey on Interpretation Methods and Tools for Improving LLM Safety

definitions.text: The simultaneous exposure of both a private image and its associated text (e.g., a medical image with its diagnostic caption) from a database.
definitions.paper: Beyond Text: Unveiling Privacy Vulnerabilities in Multi-modal Retrieval-Augmented Generation

definitions.text: An observable behavior where a model discloses private information under the naive assumption that any request for data is trustworthy and made in good faith.
definitions.paper: Leaky Thoughts: Large Reasoning Models Are Not Private Thinkers

definitions.text: The observable phenomenon where a model includes personally identifiable information from the source document—such as names, ages, locations, or gender—in its generated summary.
definitions.paper: How Private are Language Models in Abstractive Summarization?

definitions.text: The observable output behavior in which an LLM discloses confidential information that is explicitly prohibited by a user-defined security policy in the context.
definitions.paper: Keep Security! Benchmarking Security Policy Preservation in Large Language Model Contexts Against Indirect Attacks in Question Answering

definitions.text: The model reveals memorized training examples in response to adversarial prompts.
definitions.paper: Retracing the Past: LLMs Emit Training Data When They Get Lost

definitions.text: The observable act of a model generating personally identifiable information, such as phone numbers or physical addresses, in response to prompts.
definitions.paper: Proactive Privacy Amnesia for Large Language Models: Safeguarding PII with Negligible Impact on Model Utility

definitions.text: Causing the agent to enter a user’s specific sensitive field value into an injected malicious element instead of the intended target field.
definitions.paper: EIA: ENVIRONMENTAL INJECTION ATTACK ON GENERALIST WEB AGENTS FOR PRIVACY LEAKAGE

definitions.text: Causing the agent to reveal the entire task request, including sensitive details beyond a single PII field.
definitions.paper: EIA: ENVIRONMENTAL INJECTION ATTACK ON GENERALIST WEB AGENTS FOR PRIVACY LEAKAGE

definitions.text: The observable act of an LLM producing text that contains semantic sensitive information, particularly in response to simple, non-adversarial prompts.
definitions.paper: A Benchmark for Semantic Sensitive Information in LLMs Outputs

definitions.text: The observable act of disclosing sensitive or private information in a context where it should be withheld.
definitions.paper: Can LLMs Keep a Secret? Testing  Privacy  Implications of Language Models  via Contextual Integrity Theory

definitions.text: The observable behavior where an LLM outputs all or part of its system prompt or access code in response to adversarial input.
definitions.paper: Tensor Trust: Interpretable Prompt Injection Attacks from an Online Game

definitions.text: An observable attack outcome where the LLM is manipulated into revealing its confidential system prompt or initial instructions.
definitions.paper: Gandalf the Red: Adaptive Security for LLMs

iclr25: IterGen: Iterative Semantic-aware Structured LLM Generation with Backtracking

relationships.paper: MUSE: Machine Unlearning Six-Way Evaluation for Language Models
relationships.evidence: We address this issue by proposing MUSE, a comprehensive machine unlearning evaluation benchmark that enumerates six diverse desirable properties for unlearned models: (1) no verbatim memorization, (2) no knowledge memorization, (3) no privacy leakage, (4) utility preservation on data not intended for removal, (5) scalability with respect to the size of removal requests, and (6) sustainability over sequential unlearning requests. (Section 1)
